contents.AI: We conduct a thorough assessment of the precision offered by our hybrid block-sparse approach utilizing the LongBench (Bai et al., 2023) tasks, the Needlein-a-Haystack (NIAH) (Kamradt, 2024) pressure evaluations, along with the demanding RULER (Hsieh et al., 2024) benchmarks. In Table 2, we present a comparative analysis of the LongBench accuracy between our LServe system and a dense baseline. The findings clearly indicate that LServe maintains robust performance across the two models when evaluated against various test sets. Figure 9 illustrates the outcomes of the NIAH evaluations for our system, demonstrating that LServe attains a level of accuracy that parallels that of the dense baseline. Table 3 further details our testing of LServe utilizing RULER benchmarks. Unless stated otherwise, we convert half of the attention heads into streaming heads while restraining the token budget allocated for dynamic sparsity to 4096 in these benchmarks. The data in this context illustrate the performance metrics across a variety of dimensions, initiating with the benchmark comparisons for different models. For the 1vLLM 0.6.3 LServe release, the results feature a comprehensive breakdown of accuracy for various configurations, particularly when tested for sequences of increasing length, spanning from 64K to 320K tokens. The geometric mean indicates consistent performance metrics across these configurations, showcasing that LServe is highly competitive, with values generally remaining around 1.00. Notably, we emphasize the decoding speed evaluation outlined in Figure 10. The vertical axis of this figure reveals the relative throughput performance of each tested system, all normalized against the speed of LServe. It is important to acknowledge that MInference shows limited decoding capabilities due to its non-optimized decoding phase employing dense attention. When integrated into the vLLM framework, however, MInference can achieve a throughput that is quite comparable to that of vLLM, illustrating the potential benefits of optimizing various stages of attention mechanisms. Lastly, in the prefilling speed evaluation portrayed in Figure 11, we explore the differential performance of long-sequence prefilling across various serving frameworks, once again normalizing these results to LServe’s speed. Such comparisons serve to underscore the efficiency and effectiveness of our approach in handling extensive sequence inputs against other prominent frameworks in the field, offering a clear view of the advantages present in LServe’s design. Through these comprehensive evaluations, we provide robust evidence of LServe’s capabilities in efficiently managing complex tasks and benchmarks within the realm of long-sequence language model serving.

In this analysis, we utilize the same sparsity configurations outlined in Section 4.2. When compared to leading modern serving systems, LServe displays notable and consistent efficiency enhancements across a variety of GPU platforms and model architectures. Specifically, for Llama-3-8B and Minitron-4B, LServe achieves an impressive average speedup of 1.5× when set against vLLM. In the case of the MHA-based model Llama2-7B, LServe operates at an astounding pace that is over 2.0× quicker than the baseline averages. contents.AI: **Reusable Page Selection.** During the decoding process, while the attention kernel maintains a consistent level of complexity because of a limited number of historical key-value (KV) tokens, the complexity associated with the page selector, on the other hand, continues to scale linearly in relation to the sequence length. As demonstrated in Figure 14, with a sequence length set at 128K and a token budget of 4K allocated for sparse attention, the time taken by the page selector (0.24 ms) is already double that of the sparse attention kernel (0.12 ms). However, with our innovative reusable page selector integrated into LServe, we can achieve a significant reduction in page selection overhead, optimized by a factor of C, where C represents the reuse interval. Our analysis further reveals that LServe displays robustness against a variety of reuse interval selections. Table 5 illustrates that there is no considerable performance degradation until the reuse interval surpasses 8; thus, we have opted to set it at 4 by default within LServe. **Context Pooling Overhead.** To facilitate efficient page selection during decoding, it is necessary to compute representative features employing min-max pooling during the prefilling stage. It is critical to highlight that a single pooling kernel completes its execution in under 1 ms, whereas the entire prefilling stage takes about 17 seconds for a context length of 128K. Therefore, the overhead associated with context pooling becomes effectively negligible. **LServe: Efficient Long-sequence LLM Serving with Unified Sparse Attention.** Figure 15 illustrates the efficiency gains acquired through the implementation of both static and dynamic sparsity methods within LServe. The diversity in these sparsity configurations results in a cumulative speedup, where static sparsity proves to be more advantageous for shorter context lengths, while dynamic sparsity provides more pronounced benefits as context lengths extend. In Figure 15, we implement a form of static sparsity by transforming 50% of the attention heads into streaming heads. This modification results in an impressive speedup ratio ranging from 1.3 to 1.7 times, applicable across different input sequence lengths. Moreover, we explore the potential of dynamic sparsity, utilizing a fixed KV budget that accommodates 4096 tokens. This approach effectively restricts the computational complexity associated with decoding attention to a constant, yielding a remarkable speedup of 30 times when compared to the dense baseline for input lengths reaching up to 256K. contents.human: In Figure 16, we highlight the sources of performance improvement in LServe. By leveraging static sparsity, LServe achieves end-to-end speedups of up to 1.7× over the dense baseline. Additionally, dynamic sparsity, aided by a reusable page selector, significantly reduces generation latency, yielding a 7.7× speedup for sequence lengths of 256K. Lastly, LServe configures sparse patterns through offline profiling, effectively avoiding slowdowns from dynamic sparsity at shorter context lengths. 6 RELATED WORK LLM Serving Systems. Various systems have been developed to enhance LLM deployment efficiency. Orca (Yu et al., 2022) uses iteration-level scheduling and selective batching for distributed systems. vLLM (Kwon et al., 2023b) introduces PagedAttention, inspired by virtual memory, to optimize KV cache management. TensorRT-LLM (NVIDIA, 2023) is the industry’s leading solution also featuring inflight batching and PagedAttention inspired by vLLM. LightLLM (Contributors, 2023a) further reduces memory waste in PagedAttention by introducing TokenAttention. SGLang (Zheng et al., 2023) advances LLM programming with a domain-specific language and RadixAttention. LMDeploy (Contributors, 2023b) improves deployment with persistent batching and blocked KV cache. Nanoflow (Zhu et al., 2024) features intra-device scheduling and asynchronous CPU scheduling, while QServe (Lin et al., 2024b) improves LLM serving throughput through W4A8KV4 quantization and system codesign. MLC-LLM (team, 2023) accelerates deployment on edge devices via compiler-based optimizations. Inspired by contextual sparsity (Liu et al., 2023), PowerInfer (Song et al., 2023; Xue et al., 2024b) deploys LLMs on memory-constrained devices via offloading. Sparse Attention. BigBird (Zaheer et al., 2020) reduces attention complexity by blending local, global, and random attention masks. Subsequent methods like StreamingLLM (Xiao et al., 2023), H2O (Zhang et al., 2024c), and TOVA (Oren et al., 2024) simplify attention patterns by discarding KV caches mid-way through the context. However, these approaches struggle to retain the original models’ long-context capabilities due to limited global context modeling. Recent works like DuoAttention (Xiao et al., 2024), RetrievalAttention (Liu et al., 2024a), and SeerAttention (Gao et al., 2024) address this issue by introducing retrieval heads (Wu et al., 2024) or combining full attention with local attention heads. Quest (Tang et al., 2024) introduces dynamic, query-aware sparsity for accelerated decoding, while MInference (Jiang et al., 2024b) extends similar ideas to the prefilling stage. FastGen (Ge et al., 2023) optimizes decoding by profiling attention heads to discard tokens. PQCache (Zhang et al., 2024a) and ShadowKV (Sun et al., 2024) further advance the selective attention methods with product quantization and low-rank decomposition. Additionally, LongLoRA (Chen et al., 2023) finetunes shortcontext LLMs to long-context ones after converting global attention to shifted sparse attention. 7 CONCLUSION We introduce LServe, an efficient serving system for longsequence LLMs that leverages hybrid sparse attention. By incorporating unified block sparse attention, we achieve significant acceleration of the attention mechanism for both LServe: Efficient Long-sequence LLM Serving with Unified Sparse Attention 12 prefilling and decoding stages in long-sequence models. We further show that head-level static sparsity and query-aware dynamic sparsity are orthogonal and can be effectively combined with minimal impact on accuracy. LServe surpasses state-of-the-art systems, delivering an average of 1.3×-2.1× speedup in the decoding stage and up to 2.9× speedup in the prefilling stage, preserving the models’ long-context capabilities.
contents.AI: In Figure 16, we present a detailed examination of the driving factors behind performance enhancements in LServe. By effectively utilizing static sparsity, LServe is able to achieve impressive end-to-end speedups of as much as 1.7× when compared to the conventional dense baseline. Furthermore, through the implementation of dynamic sparsity, complemented by a reusable page selector, LServe substantially decreases generation latency, resulting in a remarkable 7.7× acceleration for sequence lengths of 256K. In addition, LServe strategically configures sparse patterns through offline profiling, which successfully mitigates the potential slowdowns that dynamic sparsity might introduce, particularly at shorter context lengths. 6 RELATED WORK LLM Serving Systems. Numerous systems have been designed to boost the efficiency of deploying large language models (LLMs). One such example is Orca (Yu et al., 2022), which implements iteration-level scheduling alongside selective batching specifically for distributed environments. Another noteworthy advancement is vLLM (Kwon et al., 2023b), which brings forth PagedAttention, a method inspired by virtual memory techniques that optimizes the management of the key-value (KV) cache. TensorRT-LLM (NVIDIA, 2023) stands out as an industry-leading solution that also incorporates inflight batching and PagedAttention, drawing influences from developments in vLLM. Continuing this innovation, LightLLM (Contributors, 2023a) addresses memory inefficiencies in PagedAttention by introducing the concept of TokenAttention. SGLang (Zheng et al., 2023) further enhances LLM programming by employing a domain-specific language coupled with RadixAttention. Meanwhile, LMDeploy (Contributors, 2023b) enhances deployment strategies, focusing on persistent batching combined with blocked KV cache mechanisms. In addition to these advancements, Nanoflow (Zhu et al., 2024) introduces intra-device scheduling alongside asynchronous CPU scheduling, whereas QServe (Lin et al., 2024b) increases throughput for LLM serving by utilizing W4A8KV4 quantization integrated with system design. Additionally, MLC-LLM (team, 2023) accelerates the deployment of LLMs on edge devices through compiler-based optimizations promising efficiency. Drawing from the principles of contextual sparsity (Liu et al., 2023), PowerInfer (Song et al., 2023; Xue et al., 2024b) allows the deployment of LLMs on devices with restricted memory by utilizing offloading strategies. Sparse Attention. The technique known as BigBird (Zaheer et al., 2020) mitigates the complexity associated with attention by combining local, global, and random attention masks. Following this, several methods such as StreamingLLM (Xiao et al., 2023), H2O (Zhang et al., 2024c), and TOVA (Oren et al., 2024) have aimed to simplify attention patterns by temporarily discarding KV caches as the context progresses. However, these newer strategies often struggle to maintain the long-context capacities characteristic of the original models due to their limitations in adequate global context representation. More recent innovations, including DuoAttention (Xiao et al., 2024), RetrievalAttention (Liu et al., 2024a), and SeerAttention (Gao et al., 2024), take on this challenge by integrating retrieval heads (Wu et al., 2024) or effectively merging full attention mechanisms with localized attention heads. Quest (Tang et al., 2024) presents a novel approach by implementing dynamic, query-aware sparsity aimed at speeding up decoding processes, whereas MInference (Jiang et al., 2024b) applies similar concepts within the prefilling stage of model processing. FastGen (Ge et al., 2023) optimizes decoding strategies by profiling attention heads and eliminating unnecessary tokens. Meanwhile, PQCache (Zhang et al., 2024a) and ShadowKV (Sun et al., 2024) represent further improvements in selective attention methodologies through the use of product quantization and low-rank decomposition techniques. Additionally, LongLoRA (Chen et al., 2023) refines short-context LLMs into models capable of handling longer contexts after transitioning global attention to a format of shifted sparse attention. 7 CONCLUSION In this work, we present LServe, an innovative and efficient serving system specifically tailored for long-sequence LLMs, employing hybrid sparse attention techniques. Through the integration of unified block sparse attention, we successfully accelerate the performance of the attention mechanism during both prefilling and decoding phases in models that address long sequences. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the combination of head-level static sparsity and query-aware dynamic sparsity operates orthogonally, allowing for effective amalgamation with negligible effects on overall accuracy. LServe has proven to outperform contemporary leading systems, achieving an average speedup ranging from 1.3× to 2.1× during the decoding stage, as well as boasting a substantial speedup of up to 2.9× in the prefilling stage, all while maintaining the long-context functionality of the models utilized.

contents.AI: Ainslie, J., Lee-Thorp, J., de Jong, M., Zemlyanskiy, Y., Lebrón, F., and Sanghai, S. present a comprehensive study titled “Gqa: Training generalized multi-query transformer models from multi-head checkpoints,“ which is available as an arXiv preprint with the identifier arXiv:2305.13245, published in 2023. Bai, Y., Lv, X., Zhang, J., Lyu, H., Tang, J., Huang, Z., Du, Z., Liu, X., Zeng, A., Hou, L., Dong, Y., Tang, J., and Li, J. introduced “Longbench: A bilingual, multitask benchmark for long context understanding,“ recently made accessible on arXiv as arXiv:2308.14508, also dated 2023. In another relevant work, Brandon, W., Mishra, M., Nrusimha, A., Panda, R., and Kelly, J. explore the topic of cache optimization through their paper “Reducing transformer key-value cache size with cross-layer attention,“ which can be found at arXiv preprint arXiv:2405.12981, awaiting publication in 2024. Chen, Y., Qian, S., Tang, H., Lai, X., Liu, Z., Han, S., and Jia, J. delve into fine-tuning methodologies in their research “Longlora: Efficient fine-tuning of long-context large language models,“ which is available on arXiv with the identifier arXiv:2309.12307, published in 2023. The “Lightllm: A light and fast inference service for llm“ was contributed by a group utilized a GitHub repository as a platform for sharing, accessible at https://github.com/ModelTC/lightllm, with a publication date of 2023a. Furthermore, another GitHub project titled “Lmdeploy: A toolkit for compressing, deploying, and serving llm,“ curated by a separate group of contributors, can be found at https://github.com/InternLM/lmdeploy, designated 2023b. Dubey, A., Jauhri, A., Pandey, A., Kadian, A., Al-Dahle, A., Letman, A., Mathur, A., Schelten, A., Yang, A., Fan, A., and others present their findings in “The llama 3 herd of models,“ which is hosted on arXiv under the identifier arXiv:2407.21783, set for publication in 2024. The topic of adaptive attention mechanisms is further explored by Gao, Y., Zeng, Z., Du, D., Cao, S., So, H. K.-H., Cao, T., Yang, F., and Yang, M. in their paper “Seerattention: Learning intrinsic sparse attention in your llms,“ appearing as an arXiv preprint with the number arXiv:2410.13276, which is slated for release in 2024. Ge, S., Zhang, Y., Liu, L., Zhang, M., Han, J., and Gao, J. investigate compression strategies in “Model tells you what to discard: Adaptive kv cache compression for llms,“ which is also an arXiv preprint identified as arXiv:2310.01801, published in 2023. The Gemini Team at Google offers insights into multimodal understanding in “Gemini 1.5: Unlocking multimodal understanding across millions of tokens of context,“ available on arXiv under the identifier arXiv:2403.05530, scheduled for publication in 2024. Goyal, T., and Durrett, G. analyze evaluation metrics in “Evaluating factuality in generation with dependency-level entailment,“ which can be found as an arXiv preprint with arXiv:2010.05478, published in 2020. The efficiency of large language models is examined by Hooper, C., Kim, S., Mohammadzadeh, H., Mahoney, M. W., Shao, Y. S., Keutzer, K., and Gholami, A. under the title “Kvquant: Towards 10 million context length llm inference with kv cache quantization,“ positioned as arXiv preprint arXiv:2401.18079, which is set to be published in 2024. Following closely, Hsieh, C.-P., Sun, S., Kriman, S., Acharya, S., Rekesh, D., Jia, F., Zhang, Y., and Ginsburg, B. contribute to the discussion with “Ruler: What’s the real context size of your long-context language models?“ released on arXiv under the preprint arXiv:2404.06654, with a publication date in 2024. Huang, L., Cao, S., Parulian, N., Ji, H., and Wang, L. offer strategies for document summarization through “Efficient attentions for long document summarization,“ which is available at arXiv with the identifier arXiv:2104.02112, published in 2021. The development of the Mistral 7b model is addressed by Jiang, A. Q., Sablayrolles, A., Mensch, A., Bamford, C., Chaplot, D. S., Casas, D. d. l., Bressand, F., Lengyel, G., Lample, G., Saulnier, L., and others, appearing on arXiv as preprint arXiv:2310.06825 from 2023. An innovative approach to model collaboration is explored by Jiang, A. Q., Sablayrolles, A., Roux, A., Mensch, A., Savary, B., Bamford, C., Chaplot, D. S., Casas, D. d. l., Hanna, E. B., Bressand, F., among others, in their publication “Mixtral of experts,“ designated as arXiv preprint arXiv:2401.04088, anticipated for release in 2024a. Jiang, H., Li, Y., Zhang, C., Wu, Q., Luo, X., Ahn, S., Han, Z., Abdi, A. H., Li, D., Lin, C.-Y., and their co-authors present “Minference 1.0: Accelerating pre-filling for long-context llms via dynamic sparse attention,“ available on arXiv under the identification arXiv:2407.02490, which is awaiting publication in 2024b. Kamradt, G. shares practical insights in “Llmtest needleinahaystack: Doing simple retrieval from llm models at various context lengths to measure accuracy,“ accessible via the GitHub repository at https://github.com/gkamradt/LLMTest NeedleInAHaystack, released in 2024. Kwon, W., Li, Z., Zhuang, S., Sheng, Y., Zheng, L., Yu, C. H., Gonzalez, J., Zhang, H., and Stoica, I. provide a thorough evaluation of memory optimization techniques in their work “Efficient memory management for large language model serving with pagedattention,“ which appears in the proceedings of the 29th Symposium on Operating Systems Principles, on pages 611-626, published in 2023a. In a similar vein, another contribution by Kwon et al., also titled “Efficient memory management for large language model serving with pagedattention,“ is documented in the proceedings of the ACM SIGOPS 29th Symposium on Operating Systems Principles, designated as 2023b. Li, R., Allal, L. B., Zi, Y., Muennighoff, N., Kocetkov, D., Mou, C., Marone, M., Akiki, C., Li, J., Chim, J., and additional co-authors present “Starcoder: may the source be with you!“ published on arXiv as preprint arXiv:2305.06161 in 2023. Lin, J., Yin, H., Ping, W., Molchanov, P., Shoeybi, M., and Han, S. contribute significantly to the domain of visual language models through their paper “Vila: On pre-training for visual language models,“ presented at the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition, spanning pages 26689-26699, scheduled for publication in 2024a. Lin, Y., Tang, H., Yang, S., Zhang, Z., Xiao, G., Gan, C., and Han, S. demonstrate advancements in LLM serving efficiency with “Qserve: W4a8kv4 quantization and system co-design for efficient llm serving,“ which is available as an arXiv preprint at arXiv:2405.04532, anticipated for publication in 2024b. Liu, D., Chen, M., Lu, B., Jiang, H., Han, Z., Zhang, Q., Chen, Q., Zhang, C., Ding, B., Zhang, K., and their collaborators examine the acceleration of inference in “Retrievalattention: Accelerating long-context llm inference via vector retrieval,“ also published under the identifier arXiv:2409.10516, set for 2024a. Liu, H., Li, C., Wu, Q., and Lee, Y. J. focus on visual instruction tuning in their work, noted in the Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, vol. 36, scheduled for 2024b. Liu, Z., Wang, J., Dao, T., Zhou, T., Yuan, B., Song, Z., Shrivastava, A., Zhang, C., Tian, Y., Rè, C., among other authors, investigate the implications of contextual sparsity in their paper titled “Deja vu: Contextual sparsity for efficient llms at inference time,“ presented at the International Conference on Machine Learning, covering pages 22137-22176 within the PMLR, published in 2023. Liu, Z., Yuan, J., Jin, H., Zhong, S., Xu, Z., Braverman, V., Chen, B., and Hu, X. introduce “Kivi: A tuning-free asymmetric 2bit quantization for kv cache,“ found as an arXiv preprint under the identifier arXiv:2402.02750, designated for 2024c. Lozhkov, A., Li, R., Allal, L. B., Cassano, F., Lamy-Poirier, J., Tazi, N., Tang, A., Pykhtar, D., Liu, J., Wei, Y., along with various contributors, highlight key advancements in “Starcoder 2 and the stack v2: The next generation,“ published as an arXiv preprint identified as arXiv:2402.19173 in 2024. Muralidharan, S., Sreenivas, S. T., Joshi, R., Chochowski, M., Patwary, M., Shoeybi, M., Catanzaro, B., Kautz, J., and Molchanov, P. focus on compact language model architecture in “Compact language models via pruning and knowledge distillation,“ available as CoRR preprint format/2407.14679, expected for publication in 2024. NVIDIA introduces “TensorRT-LLM: A TensorRT Toolbox for Optimized Large Language Model Inference,“ available through the URL https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM, dated 2023. OpenAI announced the launch of “openai o1“ which can be accessed at https://openai.com/o1/, marked for 2024. Oren, M., Hassid, M., Adi, Y., and Schwartz, R. present findings in their paper “Transformers are multi-state rnns,“ which is also an arXiv preprint, identified as arXiv:2401.06104, slated for 2024. Pekelis, L., Feil, M., Moret, F., Huang, M., and Peng, T. provide insights into long contextual models in “Llama 3 gradient: A series of long context models,“ released on the URL https://gradient.ai/blog/scaling-rotational-embeddings-for-long-context-language-models in 2024. Qin, Y., Li, X., Zou, H., Liu, Y., Xia, S., Huang, Z., Ye, Y., Yuan, W., Liu, H., Li, Y., and Liu, P. offer their examination in “O1 Replication Journey: A Strategic Progress Report - Part 1,“ which is available as an arXiv preprint with the identifier arXiv:2410.18982, noted for publication in 2024. Song, Y., Mi, Z., Xie, H., and Chen, H. take a look at practical applications in “Powerinfer: Fast large language model serving with a consumer-grade GPU,“ available under the identifier arXiv preprint arXiv:2312.12456, published in 2023. Sun, H., Chang, L.-W., Bao, W., Zheng, S., Zheng, N., Liu, X., Dong, H., Chi, Y., and Chen, B. emphasize performance in their work “Shadowkv: Kv cache in shadows for high-throughput long-context llm inference,“ presented as an arXiv preprint with the number arXiv:2410.21465, which is earmarked for 2024. Tang, J., Zhao, Y., Zhu, K., Xiao, G., Kasikci, B., and Han, S. discuss innovative approaches in “Quest: Query-aware sparsity for efficient long-context llm inference,“ as found in arXiv with the identification arXiv:2406.10774, scheduled for 2024. Additionally, the MLC-LLM team, noted for their contributions in 2023, has a repository that can be accessed at https://github.com/mlc-ai/mlc-llm. Touvron, H., Martin, L., Stone, K., Albert, P., Almahairi, A., Babaei, Y., Bashlykov, N., Batra, S., Bhargava, P., Bhosale, S., and their collaborators introduce “Llama 2: Open foundation and finetuned chat models,“ which is published on arXiv as a preprint, identified as arXiv:2307.09288 in the year 2023. Wei, J., Wang, X., Schuurmans, D., Bosma, M., Xia, F., Chi, E., Le, Q. V., Zhou, D., among others, make strides in evaluation methodologies with “Chain-of-thought prompting elicits reasoning in large language models,“ appearing in the Advances in neural information processing systems, volume 35, pages 24824-24837, published in 2022. Wu, W., Wang, Y., Xiao, G., Peng, H., and Fu, Y. probe the links between retrieval mechanisms and factuality in “Retrieval head mechanistically explains long-context factuality,“ an arXiv preprint indexed as arXiv:2404.15574, anticipated for release in 2024. Xiao, G., Tian, Y., Chen, B., Han, S., and Lewis, M. reveal effective streaming methods in “Efficient streaming language models with attention sinks,“ hosting their findings in a preprint available on arXiv under the identifier arXiv:2309.17453 from 2023. Finally, Xiao, G., Tang, J., Zuo, J., Guo, J., Yang, S., Tang, H., Fu, Y., and Han, S. present their work on hybrid attention in “Duoattention: Efficient long-context llm inference with retrieval and streaming heads,“ which is set to be published under the identifier arXiv:2410.10819, expected in 2024. Xue, F., Chen, Y., Li, D., Hu, Q., Zhu, L., Li, X., Fang, Y., Tang, H., Yang, S., Liu, Z., and their co-authors analyze video contextualization in “Longvila: Scaling long-context visual language models for long videos,“ published as an arXiv preprint under the identifier arXiv:2408.10188, slated for 2024a. In addition, Xue, Z., Song, Y., Mi, Z., Chen, L., Xia, Y., and Chen, H. discuss the feasibility of mobile applications in “Powerinfer-2: Fast large language model inference on a smartphone,“ which appears on arXiv as a preprint identified as arXiv:2406.06282 in 2024b. Lastly, Yu, G.-I., Jeong, J. S., Kim, G.-W., Kim, S., and Chun, B.-G. detail their distributed system approach in “Orca: A distributed serving system for Transformer-Based generative models,“ which was presented at the 16th USENIX Symposium on Operating Systems Design and Implementation (OSDI ’22), covering pages 521-538 in Carlsbad, CA, dated July 2022. The USENIX Association publishes this work, which is indexed under ISBN 978-1-939133-28-1 and can be explored further through the URL https://www.usenix.org/conference/osdi22/presentation/yu. Zaheer, M., Guruganesh, G., Dubey, K. A., Ainslie, J., Alberti, C., Ontanon, S., Pham, P., Ravula, A., Wang, Q., Yang, L., and their collaborators tackle the challenging topic of long sequence processing in “Big bird: Transformers for longer sequences,“ which appears as a significant contribution in the Advances in neural information processing systems, volume 33, pages 17283-17297, published in 2020. Zhang, H., Ji, X., Chen, Y., Fu, F., Miao, X., Nie, X., Chen, W., and Cui, B. delve into quantization methodologies in their work “Pqcache: Product quantization-based kvcache for long context llm inference,“ available on arXiv under preprint arXiv:2407.12820, identified for publication in 2024a. Zhang, T., Ladhak, F., Durmus, E., Liang, P., McKeown, K., and Hashimoto, T. B. present their findings on benchmarking in “Benchmarking large language models for news summarization,“ published in the Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics, volume 12, pages 39-57, scheduled for 2024b. Zhang, Z., Sheng, Y., Zhou, T., Chen, T., Zheng, L., Cai, R., Song, Z., Tian, Y., Rè, C., Barrett, C., and several others introduce their innovative approach in “H2o: Heavy-hitter oracle for efficient generative inference of large language models,“ included in the Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, volume 36, set for 2024c. Zheng, L., Yin, L., Xie, Z., Huang, J., Sun, C., Yu, C. H., Cao, S., Kozyrakis, C., Stoica, I., Gonzalez, J. E., Barrett, C., and Sheng, Y. focus on programming implications in “Efficiently programming large language models using sglang,“ featured in 2023. Lastly, Zhu, K., Zhao, Y., Zhao, L., Zuo, G., Gu, Y., Xie, D., Gao, Y., Xu, Q., Tang, T., Ye, Z., and their co-authors work on optimizing performance in “Nanoflow: Towards optimal large language model serving throughput,“ recently posted as an arXiv preprint identified as arXiv:2408.12757, anticipated in 2024.
